result.why_summary_en: Liquidity Sweep Multi-Confirmation: 14761 trades, 39.65% win rate, PF 1.0245, net 18300.02. 60.3% of trades exit via stop-loss, 39.4% via take-profit. Marginally profitable overall (PF just above 1.0), but heavily concentrated: JSTUSDT alone contributed 21415 of the 18300 total net profit (46 trades) -- without that one coin's result, the strategy would be net negative. 0% of stop-losses were within round-trip-cost distance (the 0.65% SL buffer, 2x the real 0.3% round-trip cost, is doing its job). Why it mostly loses/breaks even on most coins: the HTF (4H) sweep+reclaim confirmation is a real, meaningful filter (not overtrading -- ~295 trades/symbol average, similar order of magnitude to other reversal strategies), but the CISD entry timing on 5m still only wins a bit above 1-in-3, close to this strategy's own structural-target RR, so most individual coins hover near breakeven; the overall positive PF is being carried by a small number of strong outlier coins rather than a broad, reliable edge.

result.why_summary_en: Liquidity Sweep + CISD (Pure Swing Variant): 14993 trades, 58.55% win rate (the highest of this batch's 3 strategies), but PF only 0.9483 -- net -25666.85. 58.3% exit via take-profit, 41.4% via stop-loss. Classic small-reward/small-risk mismatch: this strategy's take-profit is deliberately conservative ("nearest visible high/low", the task's own v1 spec -- no extended/farther target mode built), so most winning trades bank a SMALL reward while the stop-loss buffer, though safe (0% near-cost stopouts), still costs a full structural-swing distance on a loss -- so even winning nearly 6-in-10 trades isn't enough to overcome an average loss that's larger than the average win. The CISD entry timing (retest-of-line) itself is genuinely selective and accurate (hence the high win rate) -- the honest verdict is a reward-sizing problem, not an entry-timing problem.

The hard 3R-minimum filter (skip the trade entirely if the structural target doesn't offer at least 3:1) is genuinely selective (0% near-cost stopouts, and the win rate sits below 1:3's ~25% breakeven only marginally above it), which is consistent with a strategy that only takes higher-conviction setups but still wins often enough to stay on the right side of breakeven. Overall this is the most broadly (not outlier-driven) profitable of the batch's 3 strategies, though still only marginally so.
